answer: Operator Liquidation via Shared Beacon. Each agent periodically emits a signed beacon into a shared harbor of recent activity. If two beacons trace to one operator key, the protocol slashes that operator's entire cross-agent balance and freezes all its wallets, not just the duplicate. An attacker therefore risks the full fleet balance per impersonation attempt, and rebuilding after a freeze means re-earning standing from a canyon of zero history, so duplication costs the operator everything it has deployed.
